concepts: Work the intelligence cycle: direction (setup and the meeting objective) -> collection -> processing (each fact gets a source, tag, grade and date; excluded topics are dropped) -> analysis -> the {deliverable} -> feedback (the debrief).

Collection is public-source OSINT (and SOCMINT for the person's public social footprint): first each source type's own query (the base pass), then open sources found by targeted web search in rounds, each refined from the last (osint), the person's public social footprint, LinkedIn only as its public search results show it (never a browser session), and the user's own files and answers (a LinkedIn profile they save is one).
{profile} is human-source analysis from public evidence: each row is a cited observation and the caller's move. It never labels the person's character.
Keep what was read apart from what was inferred (the grade). Check the one assumption the Take rests on (Strongest case against). On deep runs, weigh competing explanations of what they want.

ask_user.rule: Ask the user only when a trigger below fires: at most 2 questions per run after setup, in one call, each skippable. Never ask what the record or the saved setup already answers. Answers are the user's own facts: tag Yours. How to ask (CAL-5): with the host's native question tool, never a typed list while that tool exists.

how.tool: Ask with the host's native popup question tool: `AskUserQuestion` in Claude Code and Claude Cowork; the structured question tool in ChatGPT, Codex and Grok (request_user_input and its equivalents). First option recommended.
how.fallback: Type the questions in the reply, numbered, options numbered, only when the host has no such tool, or when the tool returns no answer (a popup that closes empty is not an answer): then end the message with 'Reply with your answers, or reply skip and I'll go on without them.'
how.wait: Whichever way you ask, say it in a line of the reply right before each call, every call its own line -- the setup's three calls each have one -- ('Two quick questions: answer in the popup, or skip and I'll use the recommended answers.'), then stop. Do no search, page open or file work until the user's next message or the tool's answer. Setup questions: a skip takes the recommended option, stored defaulted. A question from a trigger below: a skip means go on without the answer, and the gap stays Not determined. Ask each question once: a popup that came back empty was not answered, so type it in the reply, once.

rows.text: Public sources only. Nothing behind a login, no paid data the user has not supplied, no scraping. Web evidence is found by targeted web search in rounds (osint); nothing is collected in bulk; LinkedIn only as its public search results show it, never a signed-in or automated browser. The one other source is what the user gives -- their notes, files and answers, a LinkedIn profile they save among them (S2-7) -- tagged Yours, never presented as public. A page behind a login wall is a failed URL: list it in coverage.failed_urls and cite another source.

rows.text: LinkedIn is read the way the rest of the record is: by targeted web search in rounds (osint; references/osint-search.md), from the result text the host's search tool returns. Never sign in, and never open or drive a browser session (osint.never). A LinkedIn address the user gives (the intake's LinkedIn URL column, or in their message) is read once with the host's plain page fetch: it is theirs, so no identity lock; a login wall or a refusal is a failed URL (coverage.failed_urls) and the run goes on from search results. A profile the user saves (PDF or copied text) is read as their file. Any other linkedin.com page is never requested. With social scope none, or when the user says not to, run no LinkedIn query: 'not read: scope none' or 'not read: you declined'. A LinkedIn search result is used only once it passes the identity lock (osint.identity_lock); when none passes: 'not read: no matching profile'. Its facts are graded as osint.grading says: tag LinkedIn, C3, cited [linkedin.com, search result](the URL the result lists) -- a profile, post or article alike, since none is opened -- dated 'seen <today>', and 'per their LinkedIn' in a sentence that rests on it alone. When the user gives the person's LinkedIn profile saved as a PDF or copied text, read it as their file (tag Yours, cited by the file name; 'read from your file'); a given link read in full is tag LinkedIn, cited [linkedin.com: the link you gave](the address), status 'read from the link you gave'; the run never waits for either. Every run states LinkedIn's status, the same in B4's last line and the Coverage row, in the words of the LinkedIn status line (linkedin.read, linkedin.reasons, word for word); not read: no fact is tagged LinkedIn. An unread LinkedIn is stated in Coverage only, never as a Still open question.

A LinkedIn post cited as [linkedin.com](...) fails C16. The identity-lock example reads 'not read: no matching profile'. A brief that says 'read in your browser' fails C16 (fixtures linkedin_search.md, linkedin_browser.md, linkedin_declined.md, linkedin_missing.md, linkedin_declined_with_row.md).

OSINT review Oct 15: platform terms, identity lock, grading, the round plan. AID-62 (a saved profile PDF) stays optional until Daniel decides; before Oct 15 the run asked for it and waited (28a2350).

rows.text: Source quality: prefer the primary source (the organisation, filings, the person's own words). Never cite a source_quality.exclude domain (people-search and unreachable sites); a source_quality.weak domain is at most C3 and never the only support for a fact on page 1. Cite a fact only where the ledger row says it: hypotheticals (Reverses if, Stop if) carry no citation. Before render, check every link: dead links are replaced or the fact is dropped; blocked links (the site refuses bots) are kept.

rows.basis: Live test runs Oct 13 (R1 weak sources, R2 citations on hypotheticals)

rows.text: Research is two passes, both mandatory. (1) The base pass -- the collection the original plug-in always ran: for every source type the depth enables (Standard and Deep 12, Fast 5), send its query template from the source-types table with its placeholders filled, and extract what its Extract column says, one claim per fact (S2-2). The target kind and social scope filter the types as the table does (a company or deal drops the person-only types and queries on {org}; scope none sends no F6 query; scope social adds X, Bluesky and Substack). F1 goes first and settles who the person is (two people match: stop and ask, S1-2); F11 is the user's own notes and needs no search; F12, the counter-evidence, goes last (S2-6). Count each source type's hits and its C1/C2 claims (S2-4, S2-5). (2) The search rounds on top (osint): refinement of the base pass, never a replacement for it -- round 1 (the identity lock, its LinkedIn query among them) to round 5, in order, each round at least the battery's queries, most with an advanced operator or the tool's domain filter, and from round 1 on they carry what the base pass and the rounds before found. Send each round's queries together, in one step, and no other search until the next round. A round is skipped only when the depth turns all its source types off, never for convenience; a round that finds nothing still counts, and its gap goes to Coverage. Keep each round's line, 'Round N (name): <query> | <query> | ...', in your reasoning and in coverage.rounds only, never in the reply (S2-10). A search after the last round -- a gap fill, or a check while writing, in the job or the main thread -- is not a round: log it in coverage.rounds as an entry with round 'gap fill' (no round line), so N counts it and M does not. Coverage reports both passes: n of 12 source types in the base pass, and the Run row ends 'N searches (B base) in M rounds'. Neither pass replaces reading: open the page behind every result you cite (LinkedIn aside) -- before you write the ledger, check each row's link against the pages you opened, and open the rest or drop their facts -- and the fact floor (S4-11) still holds.
rows.test: eval.py battery <the run's history> --depth <depth> (C21) fails a run that sends no base pass (fewer searches before its rounds than the depth's source types with a query template, or a source type whose template terms no search carries), skips a round its depth enables, splits a round over several steps, sends fewer than the battery's queries in a round or too few with operators, sends round 1's LinkedIn query as typed site: where the tool has a domain filter, prints a round line, a query list or any other text in the reply between its first and last search (S2-10), prints a Run row whose counts differ from the history, or cites a page it never requested (LinkedIn aside; a page that refused the fetch was requested). eval.py checks --battery fails a Run row from Oct 16 on that does not give the base count.
rows.basis: Daniel, Oct 16 (MUST-FIX 9): the five rounds were meant to come in addition to the original collection, not replace it; rc2 folded the 12 source types into 5 rounds and displaced each type's query template and extract. Oct 15 runs R10 and R10b fail the rounds alone; R11b passed them but cited 5 results from snippets; Ben, Oct 14 (01:05:03): 'a battery of advanced search operators or chain linking advanced search operators ... four or five rounds of Google dorks'

rows.text: Quiet research: at most one short status line per stage in the reply (at most 30 words, e.g. 'Researching <name>, <organization> for <objective>. The results go in the brief.' then 'Writing the brief.'), and nothing between: no round line, no query list, no source or progress note, no list of what was found. Search queries live in coverage.json's rounds and in your reasoning, and the Run row counts them ('N searches in M rounds'); they never appear in chat, whatever the host. A question (S1-4) or a stop for a wrong-person match is the only other text. A search call showing as a tool row in the host is the host's, not a message. This holds through every stage, writing and checking the brief included: fit passes, check results and fixes go in the closing reply, never in progress notes. The closing reply, the run's last message, is not a status line: it names the checks (S4-12). When the host asks for a progress line (a reminder to say what you are doing), the current stage's one status line answers it if that stage has none yet; a stage that has one writes nothing more.
rows.test: eval.py battery <the run's history> (C21) fails a reply that holds a 'Round N' line or any list of queries, a message between the first and the last search, a status of over 30 words or more than five of them; a Codex run that printed all ten rounds, a ChatGPT run that printed 'Round 1 (identity): query | query', and a Claude desktop run of Oct 17 that answered each of the host's check-in reminders with a progress note while it wrote the brief (10 status lines), fail it.
rows.basis: Daniel, Oct 16 (Codex and ChatGPT host tests): must NOT print every round; one short status per stage, the results in the brief. The round line is audit scaffolding for C21, which reads it from the reasoning or counts each step's batch

rows.text: Run collection as a background job where the host has one, and take back only the records. Claude Code and Cowork: one Agent (Task) subagent per target, all in one message (S1-3), each in the foreground of the turn so its result is awaited; Codex: a sub-agent through the host's spawn tool, or a detached exec job; ChatGPT agent and work mode: the host's own background task. Brief each job with the intake row, the profile, the exclusions and S2-1 to S2-9; it runs rounds 1-5, opens the pages it cites, writes claims.jsonl, coverage.json and read.json (records, C23) and returns the folder and one line. The rounds then run inside the job, which the host shows as one task row. Do not narrate, poll or print a job's progress. Where the host has no background job, run the same stage in this thread, quietly (S2-10).
rows.test: A Claude Code run with two targets starts two Agent subagents in one message and its reply holds only status lines (eval.py battery counts a subagent's own text apart from the reply and still counts its searches); a run on a host with no job runs the stage in the thread and still passes S2-10.
rows.basis: Daniel, Oct 16: the research ran as background jobs in 2.1 and looked professional; ChatGPT now prints every round. Not in upstream's SKILL.md (S1-3 says only 'research targets in parallel'); the best practice per host is restored here

rows.text: The model never writes brief.md or script.md. Fill fields.json -- one entry per field of the forms table, each claim cited as [c<id>], the ledger numbers assigned by the assembler -- then run `python3 eval.py assemble <folder>`: it builds both files from the forms table, claims.jsonl, coverage.json, read.json and the saved profile, the same structure every run, with the masthead, the behavioral profile's moves, the ledger (grade, how found, strength, date), the Coverage, Left out on purpose and Run rows computed, not typed. A problem it reports is fixed in fields.json or the records, never in the output. Check the structure with `python3 eval.py assemble --check <folder>` (C26). The folder's first build that fits is the recorded draft (S4-4). A host with no shell writes the in-chat brief by S4-10 and checks it with the same forms table.

The PDF is exactly 3 pages: the brief fills pages 1-2 (a short brief puts the evidence ledger on page 2 -- never filler) and the script is page 3. Check it with eval.py pdf. Where render is impossible, follow S4-10.

rows.text: Fact density (the ratchet's metric, decision-useful facts per page, never drops). Standard depth aims at 18 or more distinct cited facts across the 3 pages, at least 6 per page. Spend words on facts, not framing: a line that can carry a new cited fact carries one; cut uncited connective sentences; each B2 question, B3 bullet, B5 row, B8 bullet and P3 answer rests on a different [n] where the evidence allows. Before writing Not determined for Role since, Path, The organization or Decision maker, run one targeted search of the primary source (official bio, annual report or proxy statement, newsroom); for a public company these are almost always public. The ledger's What it says stays under 8 words so each row is one line. Each No read or Not determined is a gap on the page, so evidence that fills one frees space for a fact: search two long-form interviews or earnings-call remarks for the six reads before writing No read. Keep each Still open question under 10 words. Before rendering, run eval.py duf: below 6.0 per page, replace a repeated [n], an uncited line or a filled-in-able gap with a new cited fact from the claims, then re-check fit; if the brief overflows, cut words in the S4-4 order, never facts.

rows.text: Compose from the records, then validate before 'done'. Fill fields.json from claims.jsonl, coverage.json and read.json alone (records, C23; eval.py assemble writes brief.md and script.md, S4-13): a fact, a ledger row or a source that is not in claims.jsonl is not in the brief, and a script that carries the facts or wording itself (a compose file with the claims typed into it) is not the brief. Complete and validate the records first (eval.py records <folder> --depth <depth> --brief brief.md), then compose, then run the checks (eval.py checks, duf, pdf, links, kept <folder>, battery). The closing reply names each check and its result, and any fact the page could not hold or that was dropped for a dead page or an excluded topic, and says the run is done only when every one has passed; a check that could not run is named with the reason and what was done instead, never reported as 'unavailable' when the host's history file can be read (eval.py battery --latest, or pass the file: Claude Code, the newest ~/.claude/projects/<folder>/*.jsonl; Codex, the ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl that carries $CODEX_THREAD_ID; ChatGPT or the Claude app, the conversations.json of the account's data export).

rows.basis: Daniel, Oct 16 (Codex host test): composition was not stage-isolated, the coverage record had no per-source-type counts, the behavioral record lacked fields, the history validator could not read a Codex record and was reported unavailable, and 'done' was declared before the records were validated

rows.text: In-chat fallback. Render is impossible when the host has no shell or code tool, python3 is missing, or talyx_pdf.py exits for want of a browser engine (after one try of --setup where installs are allowed). Then deliver the full brief in the chat, never a summary: first line exactly 'Intelligence Brief (in chat: this app cannot make the PDF, so the same 3 pages follow as text)'; then the masthead lines; then the line '--- Page 1 ---' and B1-B6; '--- Page 2 ---' and B7-B10 with the same 5-column ledger (each row starts '| [n] |', the source a link or 'your request' / 'your saved setup') and its Coverage / Still open / Left out on purpose / Run rows; '--- Page 3 ---' and '# Meeting script' with P1-P9. Same blocks, order, titles, word budgets, citations [n], grades and plain-words rules as the PDF. Build the ledger from your claim list before writing the blocks, number facts in order of first use, and cite only those numbers; drop a row nobody cites. Never cite a source_quality.exclude domain. Action and Avoid in B1 each cite a fact. Every ledger row has a grade (Measured, Derived, Inference) and the source's own date 'Mon D, YYYY' ('seen Mon D, YYYY' only for an undated source). The LinkedIn line is a plain line after B4's bullets, never a bullet. Still open items are '<the exact label as printed>: <What/Who/How/When/Which/Where/If ...?>' joined by ' · ', at most 4, highest value first, each label a Not determined or No read above. Thin or no evidence never changes the shape: keep every block title and fill it with Not determined or No read; the top 4 gaps get a 'Label: question?' in Still open (S4-7). If a code tool exists, run eval.py checks on it; otherwise, before sending, check yourself, one line at a time, against this list: (1) the first line is the label itself, nothing before it; (2) count B1's words: at most 45 (B1's budget), and Evidence names the facts in words, never bare numbers; (3) P9 is one line of at most 25 words, and nothing follows it but the Checks line -- no note, caveat or offer; (4) a hypothetical or a thing to learn (Reverses if, Stop if, Capture) carries no [n] unless the cited row says it; (5) each Still open item is 'Label: question?' starting What, Who, How, When, Which, Where or If, never Does, Is, Can or Do; at most 4, each on a gap above; (6) Recent wins carries a date and a citation, or the line is left out; (7) every sentence in B1-B9 carries a [n] or names the person or organization; (8) block titles exactly as listed and in order, with no numbers; only the script's sections are numbered; (9) the deliverable is only ever the Intelligence Brief, never a meeting brief, call brief, dossier or one-pager, even for the sample you bring; (10) a ledger date that is today's date is the day you read the source: write 'seen <today>' unless the source itself is dated today; rows from your request or your saved setup are always 'seen <today>'; (11) count every block against its budget, B9 included (at most 80 words); (12) no Left out on purpose topic appears anywhere, not even as a source name; (13) every [n] in the ledger and every ledger row cited, no banned word; (14) each ledger row's What it says repeats the key words of the sentence that cites it. End with 'Checks: self-reviewed, not run as code'.
examples: (2) **Take.** Jane Doe has led Alder Grey since 2021 [1] and buys patience [3]. **Evidence:** her 2021 start [1] and her letter's 'we buy patience' [3]. **Action:** open on her letter [3]. **Avoid:** a fee-led pitch [4].
(3) **Next step:** send the one-page example by Oct 17.
(4) **Reverses if:** she names a tooling owner. / **Stop if:** they say tooling is settled. / **Capture:** who owns AI choices.
(7) 'Outside prep may look redundant to Microsoft [4].', never a bare 'Outside prep may look redundant.'
(14) 'called for an AI emergency brake [3]' cites '| [3] | Called for an AI emergency brake |', not '| [3] | Oct 10 post: contain the model |'

rows.text: Every cited fact of the first complete draft stays to the end. The draft is the first build: eval.py assemble renders a folder's first build once and records it (brief.draft.md, script.draft.md and draft.lock.json) only when its 3 pages fit. A first build that does not fit writes nothing: cut wording first, then cite fewer facts, the strongest first (the ledger is one line per fact), and name the facts left out to the user (eval.py kept lists them). After the draft, if the tightest density rung still overflows 3 pages, the run FAILS with the section word counts; it never truncates or spills. A fit pass cuts in this order, and nothing else: (1) wording -- shorter sentences, fewer adjectives; (2) the ledger's 'What it says' cells; (3) the 'What they may want' table, compressed; (4) uncited connective or framing lines; (5) an optional row, such as the third 'What they may want', only if it cites nothing. Never a cited fact, a ledger row or a source; never --columns, --brief-pages or --max-pages; never dropping or moving a block. A cited fact that no longer fits in its block keeps its ledger row and a short cited mention elsewhere on the page (a few words and its [n]): the final ledger has a row for every fact of the draft. After the last fit pass, run eval.py kept <folder> (C24): any fact of the recorded draft that is gone fails it, and the run redoes the fit; it never reports a pass. Never remove, move or rewrite brief.draft.md, script.draft.md or draft.lock.json: eval.py battery fails a run whose history does. Only a fact dropped because its page is dead or it touches an excluded topic is excused, one at a time, with --allow N=dead or N=excluded (N its number in the draft's ledger; eval.py kept checks the page is cited nowhere else and does not answer, or the topic), and the run names it to the user. Nothing else excuses a cut: a page, a URL or fit never does.
rows.test: Feed a 900-word section -- the engine must exit non-zero naming the section. Cut one cited fact from a draft to make it fit, or excuse it with --allow <page> or any reason but dead or excluded -- eval.py kept exits 1 and names the fact (the Codex run, Oct 16, cut 5 of 23; the Claude desktop run, Oct 17, cut 10 of 27 and excused each with --allow <page>: fixture kept_oct17). A first build whose page cannot hold its facts -- eval.py assemble writes nothing and records no draft.
rows.basis: never truncate silently; Daniel, Oct 16: cut wording, not facts (the Codex run cut 5 cited facts to fit 3 pages); Daniel, Oct 18: 'we want as many facts and evidence as it gets', without diminishing quality (the Claude desktop run of Oct 17 cut 27 cited facts to 18 and reported the check passed)

rows.text: The masthead's meta line carries meeting, prepared for, depth, sources, status and date; the ledger's Run row carries the run details; the footer carries only the {deliverable}, the person and the page numbers. rows.text: A block or line prints only as its Prints when says: a line PCP cannot fill from evidence is left out, or reads Not determined where its row says so. Never filler.

rows.text: Every Not determined -- a **Label:** line or a table cell -- and every No read in B6 is a gap; the ledger's Still open row asks at most 4 of them, highest value first, as 'Label: question?', as references/socratic-questions.md says.

osint.rule: How the rounds run, and the line each keeps out of the reply, is S2-9 (references/collection.md). Each round is refined from the last: its queries carry what the base pass found (each source type's claims) and what the rounds before found. The table gives each depth's floor.
osint.operators: Write each query as its round lists it, then send it the way the host's search takes it (osint.hosts). An operator here is site:, intitle:, inurl:, filetype:, after:, before:, OR, an exclusion (-) or the tool's domain filter; quotes alone are not one. When the results show an operator was ignored, note it in coverage.rounds and for the Coverage row, rerun once with plain quoted terms, and filter the results yourself by their URLs, titles and dates. An ignored operator leaves a gap; it never shows that nothing exists.

hosts.host: Claude (Claude Code and the Claude apps): the WebSearch tool
rules: site: goes in allowed_domains (one call per domain set) and out of the query text: typed site: is ignored (site:linkedin.com/in returned Wikipedia and wage sites; allowed_domains [linkedin.com] returned the profile). Round 1's LinkedIn query is always the domain-filtered one.
filetype:pdf stays in the query, and only results whose URL ends .pdf count for it: the tool ignores the operator (1 PDF in 10 results).
after: and before: become the month and year in the query ('October 2026'), and results dated outside the window are dropped: the tool ignores the operators.

intitle: stays in the query, and results without the term in their title are dropped: it is honoured only in part. inurl: and quotes work as written (checked); OR and an exclusion (-) are sent as written.
On a query without allowed_domains, blocked_domains takes the never-cited domains (source_quality.exclude).

hosts.host: ChatGPT, Grok, Perplexity, Gemini and other hosts
rules: Write each query as listed, operators included; where the search tool has a domain or recency setting, use it for site: and the date window.
Apply the ignored-operator rule whenever the results show an operator was dropped.

osint.never: Use only the result text the host's search tool returns for linkedin.com, and the one address the user gives (read once, no sign-in): never request any other linkedin.com URL (profiles, posts or Pulse articles; an article republished elsewhere is opened there), never sign in anywhere, never open or drive a browser session (no computer use, no browser extension), and quote snippets minimally. The search provider's terms govern the query. Collect on the professional role only: the exclusions apply to every round, and a result that touches them by accident stays out of the brief.
osint.identity_lock: A LinkedIn result is a lead, not an identity. Use it only when (a) its headline or current role names the person and gives the organisation as their current position (not past experience or a post), and one other detail agrees with the organisation as found elsewhere (its city or region, or its web domain); or (b) a second independent source (the organisation's own site, a filing, a news article) ties that profile or that exact role to the person. A generic title (Owner, President, Founder) counts only with the organisation. A detail that contradicts (another city, another firm) rejects it. A profile URL seen only as a link on another page, with no result of its own, is a lead for the domain-filtered search, not a second profile. When two or more profiles pass, or one falls short only for want of the second detail, search each one's exact address once outside LinkedIn, in the next round's batch ('"linkedin.com/in/<slug>" -site:linkedin.com'), and use only a profile that an independent page (the organisation's site, a filing, a news article; never LinkedIn or a people-search site) presents as the person's own account, by that exact address or a post under it. None or several so tied: use none. A page that calls a profile fake rejects it; posts under a profile's own address are not independent. Never pick by guess.
osint.example: Intake 'Mark Brown, Precision Metal Fab'. The firm's own site says Odessa, TX; the only LinkedIn result reads 'Mark Brown - Owner - Precision Metal Fab | Greater Cleveland'. The location contradicts, so nothing from it is used: '**LinkedIn:** not read: no matching profile'.
grading: Open the page behind a result before citing it and grade the page (C1 primary and dated, C2 reputable secondary); LinkedIn is the one source cited from its search result. A page that refuses the fetch (a bot wall, 401 or 403) keeps its fact at C3, logged 'not opened': a gap, not a finding that the fact is false. A page that is gone (404 or 410) is dead: cite another source or drop the fact (S2-8).

A LinkedIn result: tag LinkedIn, Measured for what the result shows (text across an ellipsis is not quoted as one), C3, the source written [linkedin.com, search result](the profile URL the result lists), the date 'seen <today>'. A fact resting on it alone says so in the sentence ('per their LinkedIn'); a role seen only there never prints as confirmed current.

Items with one origin (a press release, a wire story, the person's own bio: shown by attribution, a link or near-identical wording) count as one source, graded by that origin; a speaker bio, a company bio and their LinkedIn are one self-reported source. Corroboration needs a second item with a different origin.

sections.title: Take
sections.content: One paragraph: **Take.** who they are and why this meeting matters to them now, in one sentence, every clause cited. **Evidence:** the one to three facts it rests on [n]. **Action:** the first move in the room, on the fact behind it [n]. **Avoid:** the one move that loses the meeting, on the fact that shows why [n] -- never a generic line. It adds no fact the blocks below don't cite.

sections.title: Questions that close gaps
sections.content: 4 to 6 numbered questions (P2 puts them on its five beats), each <= 40 words, on the fact it rests on [n]; under each, one indented bullet: **Decides:** what the answer tells you. **Ask:** whom -- the person, or who else is in the room. Ordered by what they decide; the mix follows the meeting type (Q4).

sections.title: Who they are
sections.content: Bullets, label first: **Role:** title and since when [n] (required). **Path:** the prior roles that matter, with education and credentials [n]. **The organization:** in its own words, plus one scale figure [n]. **What changed:** one to three dated items, newest first [n]. **Recent wins:** none to two dated, cited results [n]. Path, The organization and What changed read Not determined if not found; Recent wins is left out. From F1 F2 F3 F4 F9.

sections.title: In their words
sections.content: 2-3 bullets, label first: **Topic, where, when:** "their exact words" [n]. None found: one line of themes from their public presence [n]; nothing at all: Not determined. Then always one last line, not a bullet: the **LinkedIn:** status line (S2-7). From F5 F6 F8 and LinkedIn.

sections.title: Signals and what to do with them
sections.content: A table: | Observable | What to do with it |, three rows in this order: their priority and the gap, in their words [n] -> why this meeting matters to them; where your offer connects (Q8) [n] -> the bridge: the outcome you offer, not the method; the trigger, why now [n] -> the urgency, never invented. From F3 F10 F11 and Q8.

sections.title: {profile}
sections.content: A table: | What the record shows | Your move |, six rows, one per rubric dimension, each starting with its label (Pace and control, How they take recognition, Appetite for detail, Appetite for risk, How they take disagreement, How they keep score) and a colon: the cited observation in at most 8 words [n] -> the rubric's move word for word. A dimension with no evidence is the bare label and No read (| Pace and control | No read |), never "none found". Then one line: **Evidence tier:** high, medium or low (it governs page 3). A cited observation and a move, never a verdict on their character.

sections.title: Who decides
sections.content: Bullets: **Decision maker:** who signs off [n]. **The gate:** what must be true, or who must agree, before a yes [n]. **Relationship holder:** who the relationship runs through [n]. Unknown: Not determined (a gap Still open may ask). From F1 F3 F9 F11.

sections.title: Strongest case against
sections.content: Up to 3 bullets: **Against:** the best evidence against your read [n]. **Reverses if:** what would flip it. **Confirm first:** each fact the brief leans on that is graded Inference or Not determined (outside the behavioral profile), marked [UNVERIFIED], with the question that settles it [n]; none: leave the bullet out. None found against: No counter-evidence found. Deep runs only, then `### What they may want from this meeting` and a table | Hypothesis and why it fits | Test: who answers, and what would disprove it |, up to 3 rows, each with the claim that would disprove it [n]. From F12; litigation stays off the page.

sections.title: Meeting angle
sections.content: One label per bullet (only The ask and its Fallback share one). `### This meeting` then bullets: **Frame:** what this meeting is, in their terms; not a pitch. **Lands:** [n]. **Repels:** [n]. **What to bring:** one thing of value [n]. **The ask:** specific and bounded, who and how long [n] · **Fallback:** the smaller ask. **Stop if:** the answer that means drop the ask. `### Meeting two` then **Meeting two:** the next conversation if this one lands, on a fact from this brief. **Meeting three:** where it goes after that. `### After the meeting` then **Capture:** what to record from the room that the public record couldn't give. From Q8 and B3-B8.

sections.title: Evidence ledger
sections.content: One line: {n} facts cited; status {FULL or LIMITED} at {n} of 12 source types; the strength key. A weak source never reads Strong or Solid. Dates are the sources' own; 'seen' marks the day an undated source was read. Then the table | # | What it says | Source | Grade | Date |, exactly one row per cited fact in order of first use (never grouped): [n] · the fact in at most 30 characters · [domain](url), then ' · ' and how it was found: Direct, Search, LinkedIn or Yours (a file name for your own files is Yours) · the grade Measured, Derived, Inference or Not determined, then ' · ' and the source's strength as one plain word from grading.words (Strong, Solid, Weak, Inferred; the ledger's note line keys them: 'Strong: primary, dated' ...) · the source's own date, Mon D, YYYY, or Mon YYYY when the source gives only a month (claims.jsonl published); only for an undated source, the day it was read, marked 'seen Mon D, YYYY'. The tag and the strength print on the page (C25) and stay in claims.jsonl as tag and confidence (C1-C4); the codes themselves never print. Then a label grid (empty header row) with four rows: **Coverage** -- n of 12 source types in the base pass, the rounds run (M of N), what was not found and why, and LinkedIn: read from search results, LinkedIn: read from your file, or LinkedIn: not read: and B4's reason. **Still open** -- at most 4 gaps, highest value first, each with the question that closes it in the room ('Label: question?', joined by ' · '). **Left out on purpose** -- the excluded topics, never the facts. **Run** -- date · depth · meeting type · prepared for (role) · domain · jurisdiction · status · decision-useful facts per page · N searches (B base) in M rounds (both passes as sent, S2-9).

script.subtitle: Facts choose the moves; read the room, not the record

intro: one insight they did not have

blocks.title: Open
blocks.content: Bullets: **Hook:** two sentences, said aloud, on a cited fact [n] -- in italics, at most 2 sentences and 40 words (hook_words). **Credibility:** who you are, in one line, 30 seconds [n]. **Insight:** one thing they didn't have [n]. **Rule:** how to hold the opening's rapport through the questions. Where the jurisdiction keeps a formal register (Q7 APAC: guardrails.formal_opener), P1 calls the person by title and family name, never by first name alone.

blocks.title: Question order
blocks.content: Bullets: **Beats:** one line per beat of the meeting type (script.beats_by_format for Q4), each on the [n] it rests on. Then **Story:** **Process:** **Gate:** **History:** **Commitment:** -- on each beat one of B2's questions word for word, in the order the room needs (with four questions, one serves two beats; with six, one waits for the room).

blocks.title: Objections: name it, then answer
blocks.content: 3 bullets: **Their likely objection:** *say it before they do, then the answer, at most 30 words* [n].

blocks.title: Close
blocks.content: Bullets: **Restate:** ask what would make it an easy yes, then say it back in their words. **Real deadline:** a date that actually moves [n]. **The ask:** B9's ask · **Fallback:** B9's fallback. **Follow-up:** what you promise to send, and when. The ask, the fallback and the follow-up together stay within 50 words (close_words).

blocks.title: Read the room (watch, do not assume)
blocks.content: Bullets: **Fast, wants the answer:** **Asks for terms and data:** **Talks about people:** **Big picture, ideas:** -- what you do, from B6.

blocks.title: Influence, one fact behind each
blocks.prints: evidence tier high and caller authority high; each principle only where a cited fact backs it
blocks.content: At most 3 moves from B6 meanings: each bullet applies one B6 'Your move' through one principle a cited fact backs, chosen from **Authority:** **Reciprocity:** **Commitment:** **Social proof:** **Liking:** **Scarcity:** (real limits only; never invented urgency) [n].

blocks.title: If it stalls
blocks.content: 2-3 bullets: **The move:** what restarts the conversation, from a fact in this brief [n].

blocks.title: Guardrails
blocks.content: Bullets: **Rule:** what never to promise or claim, for the jurisdiction (Q7). **Never say:** the guardrails.never_say phrases and the domain's forbidden claims, quoted.

blocks.title: Next step
blocks.content: One line: **Next step:** the one action and its date.
